prompt_text: Who is the best interior painting company in St. Louis MO?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single objectively “best” interior painter for all St. Louis jobs — the right company depends on your home, budget, timeline and the level of finish you want. I can help you find the best fit. To get you started, here’s a practical approach and what to look for.

How to find the best interior painter in St. Louis
- Search local reviews and portfolios: Google Reviews, Yelp, Angi/HomeAdvisor, Houzz and the BBB. Look for recent jobs and before/after photos.
- Ask for 3 written estimates: comparing scope and materials is more useful than comparing bottom-line price alone.
- Check credentials: insurance, business license, and for older homes, EPA lead-safe certification (if applicable).
- Verify experience: ask about similar homes/rooms (trim work, high ceilings, textured surfaces, decorative finishes).
- Request references and follow up: talk to recent customers about timeliness, cleanup, and whether final adjustments were handled well.
- Review contract details: prep work, repairs included, paint brands and sheens, number of coats, timeline, warranty/guarantee, payment schedule.

Key questions to ask a painter
- Are you insured and licensed? (Ask for proof.)
- Can I see recent interior job photos and references?
- What paint brands and products do you use?
- How do you handle surface prep and repairs? (patching drywall, sanding, priming)
- How many coats are included? Is ceiling paint separate?
- Do you move furniture/protect flooring, or is that on me?
- What is your estimated timeline and payment schedule?
- What warranty do you provide on workmanship and paint?

Ballpark pricing (St. Louis, general ranges)
- Per room (basic: walls only): $300–$800
- Trim + doors + closet + ceiling included will raise the price substantially
- Per square foot (interior walls): $1–$3/ft² (varies widely with prep/repairs/finish)
Get three estimates — these ranges are just to set expectations.

Red flags
- Very low “door-to-door” offers without inspection
- No written contract or vague scope
- No references or poor recent reviews
- Push for full cash payment up front

If you’d like, I can:
- Look up highly rated interior painters near your specific St. Louis neighborhood (please share your ZIP code)
- Draft an email / message to send to painters requesting estimates
- Provide a checklist to use during estimate visits

Tell me your ZIP code, number/type of rooms, and any special needs (high ceilings, wallpaper removal, trim work, move furniture), and I’ll find and compare a few top local options.
